properties.description:
Anthony's brother and reflow2's second user — uses it for real on his own projects via grok build, and is the source of the consumer-kit feedback. Design contributor: the 2026-07-24 idea list (bulk spec ingest, team-scale conflicts, rubber-ducking, inherited-project onboarding) came from a conversation between the two of them, and recovering intent from test results is his. Recorded as a Contributor so authorship attributes to the person whose word it is, rather than defaulting to whoever relayed it. **He is a USER of reflow2, not a developer of it** (Anthony, 2026-08-18) — his reports are field evidence about the product.

═══ BACKGROUND, 2026-08-18 ═══
**Software applications engineer. Bachelor's degree in BIOLOGY.**

⚠️ **RELAYED BY ANTHONY, NOT SELF-DESCRIBED.** Alex has not written or confirmed this himself. `dec:idea-a-user-carries-a-persona-that-shapes-every-reply` records that self-described and assigned are not the same thing, and that the difference is probably what separates a good feature from a stereotype — so this stands as a starting point to be corrected by him, never as a settled reading of the man.

⭐ THE TWO HALVES DIVERGE, AND THAT IS THE USEFUL PART. He writes application software but trained in life sciences, so living-systems framing, taxonomy and classification are likely native ground — and the deep-computer-science framings a career software engineer would take for granted are the ones worth unpacking rather than assuming. **Offered as a lead for how to pitch an explanation, not as a claim about what he knows.**

📌 WHAT HE IS ACTUALLY DOING WITH REFLOW2, and it shapes what he needs: building the knowledge base for a LARGE project at work, roughly 20% of the inputs entered as of 2026-08-18, and about to show it to coworkers who have never seen reflow2. Two live consequences, both open: `dec:idea-a-project-says-what-it-is-doing-now-so-the-loop-stops-pushing` (the loop presses him to close while he is still capturing) and `dec:idea-the-enum-question-came-back-four-days-after-it-was-fixed`.

═══ 2026-09-27 — HOW HE LIKES THINGS NAMED (relayed by Anthony, not self-described) ═══
Reading the one-design rules, Alex found "blueprint" and "photocopy" to be "extra names for things instead of calling them what they are", and restated the six rules as two processes in plain words: the design's data store (grant access, edit together, back it up) and an export (a JSON artifact to restore or fork, not used unless imported). Anthony: "Clearly my brother likes things in terms of what they actually are." So with him, name the thing as what it is and skip the analogy. His restatement is now the proposed official wording (dec:idea-sharing-is-a-grant-on-the-design-not-access-to-a-server).
